speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment, can you tell me when your symptoms started and if you have experienced any recent travel or contact with sick individuals?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history at the state fair and dark urine, have you noticed any yellowing of your eyes or skin, or passed clay-colored stools? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel; REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 38.1°C (100.6°F), Blood Pressure 110/74 mm Hg, Heart Rate 99/min, Respiratory Rate Normal. General Examination: Patient appears tired; mild scleral icterus observed. Abdominal Examination: Liver palpated 2–3 cm below the right costal margin and tender on palpation. Liver Function Panel: Hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, Leukocyte Count 11,600/mm3, Platelet Count 221,000/mm3, Urea Nitrogen 26 mg/dL, Glucose 122 mg/dL, Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL, Total Bilirubin 3.6 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin 2.4 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 72 U/L, AST 48

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Viral Hepatitis (likely Hepatitis A).

I am confident this is acute viral hepatitis given the history of fair food exposure, dark urine, scleral icterus, tender hepatomegaly, and elevated bilirubin with conjugated hyperbilirubinemia. While the liver enzymes are only mildly elevated, the clinical picture is classic. Have you noticed any rash, joint pain, or itching? Do you have a history of alcohol use or intravenous drug use? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.
